_doc: Step 0 of the rerank-oriented chopper dataset (2026-11-04, user: 'design a process of using qwen to generate a dataset to continue training mmbert … few most popular languages … topics important for reranking companies'; 'start the pilot'). Pilot = 8 languages x 5k rows; full-run shares in full_share.

areas.1: customer support / help centre: how-to steps, troubleshooting, error messages, returns, refunds, account and billing rules
areas.2: internal company knowledge: HR and workplace policies, IT instructions, procedures, onboarding, benefits
areas.3: finance and compliance: company filings, financial figures, investing, banking, tax, insurance, regulation of finance
areas.4: legal: laws, regulations, contracts and their clauses, court decisions, terms and conditions, privacy policies
areas.5: e-commerce / products: a shop or catalogue page describing a specific product for sale, with specifications, prices, sizes, variants, shipping (NOT hotel, restaurant or travel reviews)
areas.6: technical documentation / software: APIs, configuration, programming, IT systems, developer Q&A
areas.7: healthcare / life sciences: medical conditions, treatments, drugs, clinical guidelines, research findings
areas.8: manuals / manufacturing: user manuals, installation and maintenance, parts, technical specifications of machines and devices
areas.0: none of these (news, opinion, entertainment, personal blogs, fiction, sports, travel, hotels and restaurants, reviews of experiences, forums chatting, etc.)

labels._doc: 2026-11-05 user: 'span should be longer, not just purely an answer, but a material for an answer, at least some full sentence, so that model is more aware of the source, which probably should also have a tag, but model should be trained with tags and without tags'. Applies to step 4 (labelling) onward; nothing generated before it changes.
labels.span_unit: whole sentences: the answer-bearing sentence(s) plus any neighbouring sentence the answer depends on (subject, conditions, units); never a sub-sentence fragment
labels.source_tag: each passage starts with a metadata header from whatever exists: domain/url, title, date (FineWeb crawl date or a parsed publication date), author, section/breadcrumb, doc type, language. Fields are optional and vary per row; synthetic docs carry the full set
labels.tag_dropout_doc: half of training rows show the source tags, half show bare passages, so the chopper works whether or not a client sends metadata; eval reports both
labels.selection_shape: a selected fragment = the metadata header + an explicit gap marker '[…]' over the skipped sentences + the 1-3 material sentences (repeat gap + sentences when the material is in two places). The header is always kept when the passage is selected
labels._doc2: 2026-11-05 user: 'tags can have also a timestamp, title, author and/or various other metadata -> selected fragments should contain metadata, then usually skip a sentence or two, and contain the material-sentence/s'
labels.todo_pool: rr_pool.py keeps only url: add FineWeb 'date' + a title guess (first short line) before step 3; author only where the page text states it

tag_leak_audit._doc: 2026-11-05 user: 'leakage on tags has to be monitored by A/B test with no-tag snippets or some other way we used before'
build_rules: positives and distractors in one pool come from the same source kind (synthetic seed -> synthetic distractors, web -> web)
each tag field is dropped independently with the same probability for every passage, so field presence says nothing about relevance
dates/authors drawn from one distribution for all passages (cf. the 2023-xx-15 collapse)
pre_training: tag-only probe: a small classifier (logistic regression on tag tokens + field presence) predicts 'has a span' from the tag alone; must be near the base rate (cf. the 0.911 length shortcut in reph v1)
body-blind probe: same, from tag + passage length + source kind
after_training: A/B: identical eval rows scored with tags vs without; the tags may help only modestly and must not help on the no-tag arm
tag swap: tags shuffled among the 16 passages of a pool; if KEEP F1 falls below the no-tag arm, the model reads relevance from tags
tag-only: bodies replaced by neutral filler; KEEP must be ~0
